prerequisites: Prior knowledge from foundational courses in computer science, telecommunication networks, and telecommunication systems.
Basic understanding of programming languages and MATLAB.

learning_outcomes.text: By the end of the course, students will have acquired knowledge of techniques for representing, compressing, encoding, and processing digital media (audio, images, video). They will understand quality measurement metrics for digital media and be familiar with both traditional and immersive multimedia applications.

The knowledge acquired will enable students to select and apply appropriate techniques for the representation, compression, and processing of digital media. They will be able to choose and apply suitable quality measurement metrics and understand how traditional and immersive multimedia applications work.
By the end of the course, students will be able to identify the most suitable approaches and technologies for representing, compressing, processing, and measuring the quality of digital media.

Students will be able to express themselves appropriately using the correct terminology to describe digital media and their representation, compression, and processing techniques. They will have acquired a suitable technical vocabulary to communicate effectively, especially with specialized audiences.

Students will gain the ability to understand how traditional and immersive multimedia applications work and are designed. They will also develop the capacity to update their skills in line with technological advancements, understand new multimedia solutions, and adapt to new development systems.

syllabus_topics: Image compression and encoding (lossy, lossless, JPEG)
Subjective methods for Digital Media Quality Assessment
Quality of Experience for Digital Media
Objective metrics for Digital Media Quality Assessment (No-Reference, Reduced-Reference, Full-Reference)
Point cloud compression and encoding (V-PCC, G-PCC)
teaching_methods: Lectures using slides with theoretical explanations, practical examples, and in-depth exercises
assessment_rules: The final exam consists of a 2-hour written test, which includes both open-ended and multiple-choice questions. These questions may cover both theoretical concepts and practical exercises. The evaluation is based on verifying the student’s understanding of both theoretical and practical concepts covered in the course. The grading is a final score.
bibliography: Lecture notes prepared by the instructor are available for all modules.
K.R. Rao, J.J. Hwang, "Techniques and Standards for Image Video and Audio Coding, Prentice Hall PTR
Ze-Nian Li, Mark S. Drew, Jiangchuan Liu, “Fundamentals of Multimedia”, Springer
